title: Touch and Count
short: Say exactly one number for each object you touch.
trouble: Children touch one object twice or skip one while their counting words keep going.

blocks.html: You can count to 10. Now let’s count real things! Touch each one and say one number.

blocks.name: counters
blocks.cap: Tap each counter as you count. A counted one turns green and shows its number.

blocks.html: One touch, one number. Every thing gets exactly one number.
If you touch a thing twice, it gets two numbers and your count is too big. If you miss one, your count is too small. One number for each thing keeps it right.

blocks.title: Counting ducks
blocks.q: Five ducks sit in a row. Count them.
steps: Touch the first duck and say 1.
Touch the next duck and say 2. Then 3, 4, 5.
Every duck got one number, and no duck got two.

blocks.name: k-pic
blocks.cap: Your turn: tap each duck as you count.

blocks.html: Touching one thing twice, or skipping one, while the counting words keep going. Fix it by moving each thing aside (or tapping it) as you count. Then you can see what is done.
For grown-ups: Ask your child to move each counted object from one pile to another. Moving makes “one touch, one number” easy to see.

sources.name: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, Kindergarten, K.CC.B.4a: say the number names in order, pairing each object with one and only one number name
